detail.longDescription: Inspired by the "If you stop writing code, you also get worse at reviewing it" thread on r/programming and "We promoted developers into architects without informing them" here. Agent diffs mostly look fine. But once you stop writing that kind of code yourself, you lose the "how would I have done this" baseline, so it gets harder to spot what's wrong. The first thing to go seems to be judgment, not typing speed. The only thing I can think of is hand-writing core pieces now and then and diffing against the agent's version. What's working for you?
